name: rosetta-consecutive-primes-with-ascending-or-descending-differences

use default

primes_below(limit: int) -> Pipe[int] is
    let composite = LIST(limit)

    for _ in 0..limit do
        composite.add(false)
    od

    for candidate in 2..limit do
        if !composite[candidate] then
            yield candidate

            let multiple mut = candidate * 2

            while multiple < limit do
                composite[multiple] = true
                multiple = multiple + candidate
            od
        fi
    od
si

longest_run(primes: Collections.List[int], keeps_going: (int, int) -> bool)
        -> Collections.List[int] is
    let best mut = (start = 0, length = 1)
    let start mut = 0

    for index in 2..primes.count do
        let previous_gap = primes[index - 1] - primes[index - 2]
        let gap = primes[index] - primes[index - 1]

        if !keeps_going(previous_gap, gap) then
            start = index - 1
        fi

        if index - start + 1 > best.length then
            best = (start, index - start + 1)
        fi
    od

    return primes[best.start..best.start + best.length]
si

let primes = primes_below(1_000_000) |> collect_list()

show(name: string, run: Collections.List[int]) =>
    write_line("{name}: {run |> map(p => "{p}") |> join(" ")}")

show("ascending", longest_run(primes, (before, after) => before < after))
show("descending", longest_run(primes, (before, after) => before > after))
